question: Why does GRPO become unstable when training large (MoE) language models with long responses, and does a sequence-level importance ratio fix it?
hypothesis: The unit of the optimization objective should match the unit of reward, so a sequence-level importance ratio and clipping will be more stable and efficient than GRPO's token-level ones.
contributions: GSPO: sequence-likelihood importance ratio with sequence-level clipping, rewarding and optimization
GSPO-token: a token-level-advantage variant numerically identical to GSPO when advantages are equal
Stabilizes MoE RL training without Routing Replay
Potential to simplify RL infrastructure by using inference-engine likelihoods

method.summary: GSPO replaces GRPO's per-token importance ratio with a length-normalized sequence ratio s_i=(pi_theta(y|x)/pi_old(y|x))^(1/|y|) and clips whole responses. Compared against GRPO (with Routing Replay) on a cold-start model fine-tuned from Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base, reported as training curves only.
method.task: RL for LLM reasoning (math and code) with verifier rewards

datasets.name: RL query set (unnamed)
datasets.preprocessing: query set regularly updated during training; not described further

training.objective: GSPO Eq. 5 with group advantage Eq. 6 and ratio Eq. 7; KL term omitted from the exposition; reward r(x,y) in [0,1] from a verifier
training.batch_size: rollout batch split into 4 mini-batches per gradient updates (rollout batch size not given)
training.compute: x-axis 'Training Compute' in Fig 1 has no units

inference.samples: AIME'24 average Pass@1 over 32 samplings; LiveCodeBench average Pass@1 over 8 samplings

eval.protocol: Training curves in figures only (values read from axes); no tables, no seeds or significance reported.

evidence.quote: we set the left and right clipping ranges in Equation (5) to 3e-4 and 4e-4, respectively

results.claim: GSPO clips about two orders of magnitude more tokens than GRPO yet trains more efficiently.
results.setup: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base cold-start RL, average over training; assignment of 0.15 to GSPO and 0.0013 to GRPO read from Fig 2 labels plus text
results.quote: we observe a difference of two orders of magnitude in the fractions of clipped tokens between GSPO and GRPO
results.note: Fig 2 prints only the numbers 0.0013 and 0.15 without attributing them in text; attribution inferred from the text.

results.claim: About 10% of activated experts differ after each gradient update for the same rollout, which destabilizes GRPO's token ratios.
results.setup: 48-layer Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base, per RL gradient update, same rollout sample
results.quote: there are roughly 10% of the experts activated under the new policy
results.note: 'roughly'; more prominent in deeper MoE models.

results.claim: GSPO trains stably and beats GRPO (w/ Routing Replay) on training reward, AIME'24, LiveCodeBench and CodeForces at equal compute; no numeric table.
results.setup: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base cold-start, Fig 1 axes roughly 0.50-0.70 reward, AIME'24 70-80, LCB 55-65, CodeForces 1800-2000; single runs
results.quote: GSPO also demonstrates superior training efficiency over GRPO, achieving better training accuracy and benchmark performance under the same training compute and consumed queries.

results.claim: Without Routing Replay, GRPO MoE training does not converge normally; GSPO needs no Routing Replay.
results.quote: Figure 3 demonstrates that Routing Replay serves as an essential technique in the normal convergence of the GRPO training of MoE models.

results.claim: GSPO may allow using inference-engine likelihoods directly, avoiding recomputation; stated intuitively, not tested.
results.quote: intuitively, the former is much more tolerant of precision discrepancies

results.claim: GRPO collapse is attributed to misapplied token-level importance weights; collapse is irreversible even after reverting checkpoints or tuning clip ranges.
results.quote: We have empirically observed that this can lead to model collapse that is often irreversible.

limits: Evidence is training curves for one model; no tables, seeds, or error bars
Baseline is GRPO with Routing Replay; no comparison with other stabilizers (e.g. DAPO) or dense models
Hyperparameters (learning rate, group size, batch size, steps, data, hardware) not given
Infrastructure benefit (Sec 5.4) is argued intuitively, not measured
Authors built GSPO and used it for Qwen3; collapse mechanism not isolated by ablation
Training Compute axis has no units

terms.definition: token-level objective variant with s_i,t = sg[s_i]*pi_theta(y_t)/sg[pi_theta(y_t)], allowing per-token advantages
cache the experts activated in pi_old and replay these routing modes in pi_theta when computing importance ratios

lineage.note: GSPO used in latest Qwen3 models; Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base is the base
